hooks.text: The most famous labor strike in history didn't even happen on Earth.
An accidental radio error caused a ninety-minute communications blackout in orbit.
Did three exhausted astronauts really go on strike in space?

title: The Space Mutiny That Never Happened
description: The real story behind the Skylab 4 strike and the accidental radio error that fooled the world.

beats.text: In November 1973, NASA launched three rookie astronauts to America's first space station, Skylab.
beats.visual: photograph of the launch of Skylab 4 on a Saturn IB rocket, 1973

beats.text: Gerald Carr, Edward Gibson, and William Pogue soon struggled under an incredibly micromanaged eighty-four-day schedule.
beats.visual: photograph of the Skylab space station in Earth orbit, 1973

beats.text: When the astronauts tried to hide an early case of space sickness, NASA’s chief astronaut Alan Shepard issued a stern reprimand.
beats.visual: photograph of Alan Shepard in his Apollo 14 spacesuit, 1971

beats.text: Exhausted and overworked, the crew suffered an accidental radio error that caused them to miss a scheduled daily briefing.
beats.visual: photograph of Edward Gibson conducting a spacewalk outside Skylab, 1973

beats.text: This ninety-minute radio gap was immediately sensationalized by the media as a deliberate and unprecedented mutiny in orbit.
beats.visual: photograph of the Apollo Telescope Mount solar observatory on Skylab, 1973

beats.text: After the schedule was lightened, the crew became more productive than ever, yet none of them ever flew in space again.
beats.visual: photograph of the official Skylab 4 mission patch, 1973
